gen-gf-noto-serif-lao-fs-asap: Soft, old-school headlines meet a lean body. Noto Serif Lao has a mild swell in its bowls, while Asap keeps its c forms open and its lowercase tall against the capitals. Serif warmth leads; sans clarity follows.
gen-gf-noto-serif-lao-fs-epilogue: Epilogue brings curvy, wire-thin sans letters with a tall lowercase and stubby ascenders, set under Noto Serif Lao. Epilogue also works comfortably a size or two below the heading, where its monoline skeleton stays crisp.
gen-gf-noto-serif-lao-fs-fira-sans: Gently tilted-nib strokes give Noto Serif Lao its traditional, softly shaded look. Fira Sans replies with a laser-straight line of constant width and a generous x-height, so the heading carries the character and the body carries the text.
gen-gf-noto-serif-lao-fs-public-sans: Public Sans brings a hefty lowercase and broad counters, tucked beneath Noto Serif Lao and its hairlines that stay visible without turning brittle. Paragraphs would feel sturdy and unhurried.
gen-gf-noto-serif-lao-fs-supreme: Supreme sets a thick, dense band of sans text. Noto Serif Lao does its best work with gentle stroke variation and a traditional feel, while Supreme is at its best keeping every letter crisp and open.
gen-gf-noto-serif-lao-general-sans: Traditional shape, modern backbone. Noto Serif Lao's thick strokes lead the eye without taking over, while General Sans runs a ballpoint-like line with a tall x-height. They share the line comfortably.
gen-gf-noto-serif-lao-manrope: Manrope opens every curve with a bright gap. Under Noto Serif Lao's soft pencil-like thick-to-thin shifts, its steady sans line feels friendly and uncluttered, like a ruled page beside a hand-drawn one.
gen-gf-noto-serif-lao-montserrat: Montserrat lays down geometric sans curves with oversized counters and a wire-straight line. Montserrat against Noto Serif Lao's mellow swing from thick to thin gives the pair its best quality: a clear shift between old and new.
gen-gf-noto-serif-lao-satoshi: Satoshi stands tall with a soaring x-height and a wide e, cut to one width throughout. And Noto Serif Lao above it adds moderate thick and thin strokes, a traditional voice over a quiet sans.
gen-gf-noto-serif-lao-switzer: Swiss tidiness, with a soft serif lead. Noto Serif Lao's lightly modulated strokes have no harsh thin spots, and Switzer's cord-like sans curves, as heavy as its stems, give that gentleness a firm, tubular partner.
